# Dry

The `dry` slice helps find duplicate code.
It uses `jscpd`, a tool that spots copied blocks, and it helps Claude decide which copies to merge.
Less duplicate code means less to read and less to fix.

## What It Does for You

The slice adds one command and one skill.
It has no hook, no `userConfig` key, and no setting, so there is nothing to turn off.
The command `jscpd-config` writes the config of `jscpd`.
The skill `dry` tells Claude when to run `jscpd` and how to read a clone.

| Item | Kind | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `jscpd-config` | Command in `bin/` | Merges `jscpd.local.json` and its `extends` chain into `.jscpd.json`. |
| `dry` | Skill | Finds clones, reads each clone, and decides if a merge is good. |

The slice runs no `jscpd` itself.
Claude runs `bunx jscpd` after the command wrote the config.

## How to Use It

Run `jscpd-config` from the root of the project to write the config:

```text
jscpd-config [--local FILE] [--out FILE]
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--local FILE` | `jscpd.local.json` | The file with the rules of the project. |
| `--out FILE` | `.jscpd.json` | The file that the command writes. |

When the local file does not exist, the command writes the shipped base.
The command writes the output file in one step, so a failed run leaves no half file.
`--help` and `-h` print the usage and exit with 0.

## The Shipped Base

The base is `assets/jscpd.base.json` in the slice.
It sets these keys:

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `minTokens` | 50 |
| `minLines` | 5 |
| `mode` | `mild` |
| `similarity` | 0.8 |
| `semantic` | `{ "scope": "all" }` |
| `baseline` | `.jscpd-baseline.json` |
| `failOnNewClones` | 0 |
| `gitignore` | `true` |
| `reporters` | `["console"]` |

The base ignores `.git`, `node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `target`, `vendor`, minified files, and lock files.
With the baseline file and `failOnNewClones` at 0, only a new clone fails a run.
The base lists no format, so a project adds each format in `formatsExts`.
`semantic` needs a large model download, so a project sets `"semantic": null` when it does not want it.

## Merge Rules

`jscpd.local.json` can name a parent in `extends`.
The value is a path from the folder of the file, or `claudetto:base` for the shipped base.
The command merges the chain from the first file to the local file:

- A key of the child replaces the key of the parent.
- An object merges deep.
- A list under a key that starts with `ignore` appends the child items to the parent items, with no repeat.
- The key `<key>Remove` takes items out of the list of the parent.
- A value `null` deletes the key.

A chain that returns to a file is an `extends` cycle, and the command stops with an error.

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | The command wrote the file, or printed the usage. |
| 2 | A file does not parse, an `extends` chain has a cycle, or the write failed. |

## The Skill

Claude runs the skill when a change copies a block, before it finishes a change that adds many lines, and when the user asks about duplication.
The skill tells Claude to merge two clones only when one change of a rule must change both, and the behavior and the effects stay the same.
It tells Claude not to merge blocks that only look alike, or a merge that needs a flag for each difference.
A clone that Claude keeps on purpose goes in the baseline with `bunx jscpd --update-baseline`, and Claude says why.
